concept: Atlas write-blocking thresholds and Intelligent Workload Management

claims.text: Atlas Core blocks writes, including deletes, when its primary lacks disk headroom; reads continue, and sharded clusters restrict the affected shard. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For migration workloads that can contribute to disk pressure, Percona ClusterSync documentation requires destination capacity for both the full dataset and the oplog entries representing applied changes. It suggests reducing destination oplog retention or size only when extended retention is unnecessary. This is capacity-planning context, not independent verification of Atlas IWM thresholds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13)

Optional database Load Shedding is limited to M30+ replica-set clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later. The documented default setting is Atlas Managed, whose effective state on MongoDB 9.0 is Disabled. When enabled, a full bounded ingress queue causes incoming operations to be rejected with overload errors. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)
For 20 GiB–1.25 TiB disks, Atlas blocks writes below 4% free and unblocks above 6% free. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The configurable data-partition disk alert defaults to 90% used, distinct from critical write-blocking thresholds. Atlas automatically unblocks writes after recovery and emits an information-only unblocking alert. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The documented disk-size bands use distinct block and unblock thresholds: 8–20 GiB blocks below 600 MiB free and unblocks above 900 MiB; 20 GiB–1.25 TiB blocks below 4% free and unblocks above 6%; 1.25 TiB or greater blocks below 50 GiB free and unblocks above 75 GiB. These are free-space thresholds, not a universal 90% disk-used rule. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

The default configurable Data Partition disk-used alert threshold is 90% of configured storage, whereas actual write-blocking follows the separate free-space thresholds. Atlas also provides blocked and unblocked write alerts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Disk write-blocking also blocks document deletes, because deleting documents can temporarily increase used disk space. A delete-based emergency cleanup therefore cannot be assumed to work once this protection has engaged. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)
For 8–20 GiB disks, Atlas blocks writes below 600 MiB free and unblocks above 900 MiB free. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
For disks of at least 1.25 TiB, Atlas blocks writes below 50 GiB free and unblocks above 75 GiB free. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The documentation reports different write-blocking log messages by feature compatibility version: FCV 9.0 or later uses "Replica set writes blocked, reason: InsufficientDiskSpace"; earlier FCVs use "User writes blocked, reason: DiskUseThresholdExceeded". (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)
Write-blocking applies to M10+ on MongoDB 8.0+; optional Load Shedding requires M30+ replica sets on 9.0+. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

IWM manages resource pressure while additional capacity is provisioned; it does not add capacity or replace auto-scaling and capacity planning. A traffic spike can overload a cluster before auto-scaling completes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

A migration can consume disk faster than auto-expansion completes. Atlas recommends increasing storage or enabling auto-expansion to recover; enabled auto-expansion does not guarantee prevention of write-blocking. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas introduced eligible-cluster IWM write-blocking on 27 August 2025. Its March 2026 changelog records a switch from static to dynamic range-based thresholds to reduce unnecessary blocking during disk scaling. (low confidence)

A practitioner records a bulk restore aborting with DiskUseThresholdExceeded and recommends preallocating generous storage. This is anecdotal incident evidence; its broader claim that auto-scaling always blocks writes is unverified. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The MongoDB server master compact.cpp source calls ReplicaSetWriteBlockState::checkIfCompactAllowedToStart before a non-dry-run compact operation; dryRun bypasses that admission check. This source-level gate alone does not establish whether compact will be admitted under every Atlas disk-pressure state. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

MongoDB recommends increasing cluster storage manually or enabling storage auto-scaling to recover from disk write-blocking; Atlas automatically unblocks writes after the recovery threshold is crossed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

IWM combines always-on protections with optional Load Shedding. Disabling Load Shedding does not disable the always-on protections, which include disk write-blocking on eligible clusters. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Full IWM is active on Dedicated clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later, with protections varying by tier and topology. Disk write-blocking also applies to M10+ clusters running MongoDB 8.0 or later; Free and Flex clusters are outside IWM eligibility. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

MongoDB states that default IWM protections work with any MongoDB driver. For optional Load Shedding, MongoDB recommends a supported backpressure-aware driver and bounded retries with backoff. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-08)

Reducing oplog retention as a disk-pressure workaround can endanger CDC consumers: Hevo documents that an event not read within the retention period is lost, and recommends enough oplog space for 72 hours of retention for its connector. This is Hevo-specific operational guidance, not an Atlas write-blocking threshold. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-23)

The Atlas changelog records an improvement from static write-blocking values to dynamic range-based thresholds to reduce unnecessary blocking during disk scaling. This scopes older fixed-threshold descriptions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
